//: INTERIOR DOCUMENT for the data-shaped module `search.orderings` (search/orderings.py).
//1: Owned by Credit Risk Policy. Changing it is an INTERIOR change: staged compile + swap,
//2: no deployment, no engineer. Adding H9 (change scenario 6) is one object in `rules`.
//3: The vocabulary is closed: `key` names a column the module declares in `reads`, and
//4: `direction`, `filter.op` and `prefix` come from fixed enumerations. There is no
//5: expression language here (doc 08 3.2) - `effective_rate` is a REGISTERED step id.

rules.description: Settle the highest effective rate first. The cheapest source of client benefit: an account at 31% is worth settling before one at 14%.
rules.prefix_note: prefix_depth_rate defaults to 8 and is bounded by CON-INT-01 at evaluation.

rules.description: Settle the highest instalment relief per rand of settlement first. R800/month released for R14 000 beats R900 released for R210 000 when the binding constraint is affordability.
Settle the shortest remaining term last. An account with four instalments left releases its instalment in four months for free; settling it consumes advance and releases almost nothing.

Never include a secured account unless its security releases or transfers to the new facility. A settled vehicle finance whose security does not move leaves the Bank unsecured on a depreciating asset.
rules.constraint_note: A `constraint` rule contributes no key and no prefix. It removes accounts from EVERY ordering's candidate pool. It is authored here rather than in settleability because Credit Risk Policy owns it and revises it; settleability class 3 records the fact, this rule decides the consequence.

rules.description: Prefer accounts with a provider the client is in arrears with. Arrears are contagious across a provider relationship; settling one account of three at a provider in arrears removes a debit order but not the relationship.
Prefer accounts whose quotation is in hand and unexpired. A scenario built on held quotations is executable this week; one built on estimates is conditional.
Prefer settling a provider relationship in full over settling part of it. Leaving a R380 balance open at a provider the client has otherwise exited produces a forgotten account and a default listing.
rules.grouped_note: A `grouped` rule emits whole groups, not individual accounts: its prefix k means 'the top k provider relationships, entire'. This is the only rule kind that can produce a candidate larger than its prefix depth, which is why CON-INT-01 is enforced at evaluation and not here.

rules.description: Prefer accounts with the highest re-accumulation risk. A store card settled and left open will be re-used; where the facility cannot be closed, prefer settling it early and requiring closure as a condition.

Prefer accounts whose provider has the shortest quotation turnaround. Added 2026-06 for the branch channel, where the client is present and an executable-this-week answer is worth more than an optimal one.

seeds.description: The empty set: the do-nothing baseline, so the chosen outcome is always compared to doing nothing.
The client's nominated set exactly as nominated.
The nominated set extended by each ordering's prefixes.
The full settleable set. Frequently unaffordable, but it is the client's mental model and must be priced so it can be shown to have been.
